plugin_desc: MSSQL Exporter is used to collect and export metrics from Microsoft SQL Server databases, including query performance, connection counts, transaction statistics, and resource usage, to help monitor the health and performance of MSSQL instances.
name: MSSQL

metrics.name: sqlserver_cpu_sqlserver_process_cpu_avg
metrics.description: CPU usage by the SQL Server database process, directly reflecting database computational load. Sustained high values may indicate queries need optimization or resource bottlenecks exist.

metrics.name: sqlserver_cpu_system_idle_cpu_avg
metrics.description: Overall operating system idle CPU percentage, indicating total CPU resource utilization. Low values indicate CPU resource constraints that may affect system stability.

metrics.name: sqlserver_server_properties_uptime
metrics.description: Duration since last SQL Server instance startup, monitoring instance stability. Long uptime may require a restart to free memory and clean up resources.

metrics.name: sqlserver_database_io_read_latency_ms
metrics.description: Average latency time for database file read operations, reflecting storage subsystem performance. High latency may indicate storage bottlenecks, network issues, or insufficient hardware performance.

metrics.name: sqlserver_database_io_write_latency_ms
metrics.description: Average latency time for database file write operations, directly impacting transaction performance and application response times. High latency may affect data write speed and system throughput.

metrics.name: sqlserver_database_io_reads_rate
metrics.description: Rate of database file read operations, indicating data retrieval load intensity and working set access patterns. High read rates may indicate frequent queries or low cache efficiency.

metrics.name: sqlserver_database_io_writes_rate
metrics.description: Rate of database file write operations, indicating data write load intensity and transaction activity levels. High write rates may indicate substantial data updates or insert operations.

metrics.name: sqlserver_memory_clerks_size_kb
metrics.description: Current memory size allocated by SQL Server internal memory clerks, used to analyze memory usage distribution and identify potential memory leaks. Different clerks represent different memory usage purposes.

metrics.name: sqlserver_performance_value_rate
metrics.description: Rate of batch requests processed by SQL Server, measuring overall database throughput and load pressure. High request rates indicate the database is processing a large volume of queries.

metrics.name: sqlserver_checkpoint_pages_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which the checkpoint process flushes dirty buffer pages to disk. It reflects write-back pressure and should be interpreted together with write latency and lazy writes.

metrics.name: sqlserver_lazy_writes_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which the lazy writer flushes pages to make buffer-pool space available. Sustained growth together with low page life expectancy indicates memory pressure.

metrics.name: sqlserver_memory_grants_pending
metrics.description: Current number of queries waiting for execution-memory grants. A nonzero sustained value indicates query-workspace memory pressure.

metrics.name: sqlserver_processes_blocked
metrics.description: Current number of blocked SQL Server processes. Sustained values require checking blocking sessions, transaction scope, and lock contention.

metrics.name: sqlserver_deadlocks_rate
metrics.description: Rate of SQL Server deadlocks. Any sustained nonzero rate requires investigation of transaction order, isolation level, and indexing.

metrics.name: sqlserver_sql_compilations_rate
metrics.description: Rate of SQL statement compilations. It helps assess plan-cache efficiency when compared with batch request and recompilation rates.

metrics.name: sqlserver_sql_recompilations_rate
metrics.description: Rate of SQL statement recompilations. A high rate relative to compilations can increase CPU cost and reveal unstable plans or frequent schema changes.

metrics.name: sqlserver_memory_grants_outstanding
metrics.description: Current number of granted query-workspace memory requests that have not yet completed. Interpret it with pending grants to distinguish active workload from memory pressure.

metrics.name: sqlserver_memory_target_server_memory_kb
metrics.description: SQL Server target memory in KiB. Compare it with total server memory to determine whether the buffer pool has reached its configured target.

metrics.name: sqlserver_memory_total_server_memory_kb
metrics.description: Current SQL Server memory committed in KiB. A persistent gap below target can indicate memory pressure or a recent workload change.

metrics.name: sqlserver_tempdb_free_space_kb
metrics.description: Current free space in TempDB in KiB. Low free space can cause failures in sorting, hashing, row versioning, and temporary-object workloads.

metrics.name: sqlserver_tempdb_version_store_size_kb
metrics.description: Current TempDB version-store size in KiB. Growth can indicate long-running snapshot or read-committed snapshot transactions.

metrics.name: sqlserver_log_flushes_rate
metrics.description: Rate of transaction-log flushes. Interpret it with database write latency to identify write-intensive workloads and log I/O pressure.

metrics.name: sqlserver_page_life_expectancy
metrics.description: Average time data pages stay in the buffer pool, reflecting memory pressure. Low values suggest insufficient memory, potentially causing frequent physical I/O and impacting performance.

metrics.name: sqlserver_buffer_cache_hit_ratio
metrics.description: Percentage of data page reads satisfied from the buffer pool, reflecting memory efficiency. High hit ratios indicate most data requests are served from memory, suggesting good performance. Low hit ratios may indicate a need for more memory.

metrics.name: sqlserver_user_connections_rate
metrics.description: Number of users currently connected to the SQL Server instance, reflecting concurrent load and connection pool usage. Too many connections may lead to resource contention.

metrics.name: sqlserver_lock_wait_time_rate
metrics.description: Rate of lock waits, reflecting concurrency contention. High values may indicate blocking or lock contention that requires transaction design optimization.

metrics.name: sqlserver_requests_cpu_time_ms_rate
metrics.description: Rate of CPU time consumed by requests, used to identify queries and statements with high CPU consumption, aiding in performance optimization and resource allocation decisions.

metrics.name: sqlserver_requests_logical_reads_rate
metrics.description: Rate of logical read operations by requests, reflecting query data access patterns and working set size. High logical reads may indicate queries lacking indexes or needing optimization.

metrics.name: sqlserver_requests_total_elapsed_time_ms_rate
metrics.description: Rate of total elapsed time of requests, monitoring query execution efficiency and response times. High elapsed time may indicate complex queries, large data volumes, or performance issues.

metrics.name: sqlserver_requests_wait_time_ms_rate
metrics.description: Rate of wait time of requests, reflecting query waiting on resources. High wait times may indicate resource bottlenecks or lock contention.

metrics.name: sqlserver_schedulers_active_workers_count
metrics.description: Number of active workers currently executing tasks on schedulers, reflecting CPU scheduling load. Excessive numbers may indicate high CPU pressure or parallel query contention.

metrics.name: sqlserver_schedulers_runnable_tasks_count
metrics.description: Number of tasks ready to run and waiting for CPU execution on schedulers, reflecting CPU queue length. High values indicate insufficient CPU resources or a large number of concurrent requests.

metrics.name: sqlserver_waitstats_resource_wait_ms
metrics.description: Rate of time spent waiting for external resources (such as disk, network, memory), reflecting true resource bottlenecks. Helps identify hardware limitations like I/O, memory, or network.

metrics.name: sqlserver_waitstats_signal_wait_time_ms_rate
metrics.description: Rate of time spent waiting for CPU scheduler, reflecting CPU pressure. High signal wait time indicates CPU resource contention or parallel query issues, requiring query optimization or additional CPU resources.

metrics.name: sqlserver_waitstats_wait_time_ms_rate
metrics.description: Rate of cumulative wait time for various wait types in SQL Server, a key metric for performance tuning that helps identify system bottlenecks.

metrics.name: sqlserver_waitstats_waiting_tasks_count
metrics.description: Number of SQL Server tasks currently waiting, reflecting the system's concurrent wait situation. High waiting tasks count may indicate resource contention in the system.

metrics.name: sqlserver_volume_space_available_space_bytes
metrics.description: Available space on storage volumes, monitoring disk space usage. Insufficient space may cause database operation failures or performance degradation.

metrics.name: sqlserver_volume_space_total_space_bytes
metrics.description: Total space on storage volumes, used to calculate disk usage and plan storage expansion.

metrics.name: sqlserver_volume_space_used_space_bytes
metrics.description: Used space on storage volumes, combined with total space to calculate usage rate and monitor storage growth trends.
